ruling.reasoning:
This is a RydeX fixed-quote trip of $35.91 (F6), so the fare does not vary with distance and the trace's RD-2 check fails: even with a 1.87 km off-route segment (F3) against a billed distance of 17.0 km equal to the optimal route (F4), the amount to refund is $0.00 — the rate would be $23.91 ÷ 16.96 km = $1.4098/km, but a fixed quote is unaffected, so no money moves [F3][F4][F6][RD-2]. The refund side of the complaint therefore fails regardless of the segment finding; the complaint of an unexplained longer route does not survive the fixed-fare model [F6][RD-2].

The live issue is the single off-route segment (09:49–09:56, 1.87 km extra, F3) and whether it is excused, which decides the RD-6 account flag because the driver already has 2 upheld route disputes in 90 days (F17) [F3][F17][RD-1][RD-6]. The driver proposed the change at 09:45 and named a road — "Jam on Pan Island Expressway is building up ahead, can I go round via Bedok Reservoir Road?" (F7) — and the rider, in a timestamped message sent before the segment started, replied "Sure, go ahead." at 09:46 (F8, F9) [F3][F7][F8][F9][RD-5]. That is a rider's own specific named-road consent, not a claim appearing only in the driver's statement (F10) [F8][F10][RD-5].

Scope: agreeing to "Bedok Reservoir Road" covers driving on that road only, and the record must tie this segment to that road [F3][F7][F8][RD-5]. The fact table carries no road names for the driven path, no message places the car on Bedok Reservoir Road, and the driver's own statement names the same road rather than another place, so nothing ties the segment to the agreed road and nothing places it elsewhere — the finding is undetermined, not exempt and not a driver's errand of his own [F3][F7][F10][RD-5]. The traffic record is consistent with the driver's stated reason (PIE speed band 2, 10–19 km/h, through 09:49, F11) but a speed band alone does not exempt and no incident was recorded (F12, F13, F14) [F11][F14][RD-4]; the weather was fair (F15) and the profiles do not decide anything on their own (F16, F17) [F16][F17][RD-6].

Because the undetermined segment finding changes the outcome — an exempt segment leaves the driver clean, while a counted segment triggers the RD-6 flag — the case cannot be closed by me and goes to a person [F3][F17][RD-5][RD-6]. A human reviewer should check the trip path/telemetry to see whether the segment was actually driven on Bedok Reservoir Road. On the fare the answer is unaffected: fixed fare, no refund [F4][F6][RD-2].
